answer: Each agent first locks 64 GB of RAM and computes a Blake3 state root over its array, binding the plume of its trace to a ferrous-hard memory commitment no clone can share. The verifier issues a fresh nonce and demands the root for a slice re-derived within 90 seconds, proving live possession, not a copied hash. Peers audit the velvet public log and flag any root repeated across identities. One honest agent holds one 64 GB array; 10 fakes must hold 10 arrays, 640 GB on ten machines, scaling cost linearly. Failure slashes the bonded deposit and freezes repeat offenders.
